analysis_status: post-result hypothesis-generating held-out predictive-information decomposition; not confirmatory

definitions.plant_availability_increment: pollinator-only held-out log-loss minus the two-axis marginal-full held-out log-loss
definitions.pollinator_activity_increment: plant-only held-out log-loss minus the two-axis marginal-full held-out log-loss
definitions.gain_axis_contrast: pollinator activity increment minus plant availability increment
definitions.loss_axis_contrast: plant availability increment minus pollinator activity increment

gain.individual_axis_increment_note: both individual increments are positive_but_fold_unstable because 2006->2007 is negative for both

loss.exception_context: 2006 used an expanded site pool relative to the strict-core years and is already designated a broad sampling-effort sensitivity

ecological_read.supported: Within the repaired current-state opportunity baseline, the predictive information is not symmetrically distributed between the two marginal axes. Link gains carry more held-out information from pollinator activity on other plants, whereas link losses carry more held-out information from focal-plant flowering availability in the primary and near-core scopes.
ecological_read.hypothesis: A candidate follow-up hypothesis is that entry into an interaction is more limited by whether a pollinator is currently active in the local floral environment, whereas persistence of an established interaction is more sensitive to continued plant-side availability.
ecological_read.scope: This is an endpoint-specific predictive-information asymmetry, not a demonstrated biological mechanism.

not_established: pollinator activity causally drives link formation
plant flowering availability causally drives link loss
assembly and disassembly are proven to have different mechanisms
the axis asymmetry is independent of observational sampling effort
the 2006->2007 exception is caused by the expanded site pool rather than merely coincident with it
claim_ceiling: Post-result, hypothesis-generating decomposition of held-out predictive information only. The primary and near-core directional asymmetry is reproducible, but it must not be promoted to a causal assembly/disassembly mechanism or routeability result without independent replication or intervention.
